result.label: Source-read

claims.claim: An acknowledgment or promise is insufficient evidence of a new or continuing contract to take a case outside the limitations statutes unless it is in a writing signed by the party to be charged.
claims.quote: No acknowledgment or promise is sufficient evidence of a new or continuing contract, by which to take the case out of the operation of this title, unless the same is contained in some writing, signed by the party to be charged thereby,
claims.note: The draft states the promissory-note payment exception in the next sentence. It does not say that a signature alone restarts the period.

claims.claim: A payment on account of principal or interest due on a promissory note made by the party to be charged is deemed a sufficient acknowledgment or promise of a continuing contract.
claims.quote: any payment on account of principal or interest due on a promissory note made by the party to be charged shall be deemed a sufficient acknowledgment or promise of a continuing contract
claims.note: The draft limits this payment rule to promissory notes, not all written consumer debts.

claims.claim: Each such payment stops the running of the time to commence an action on the note.
claims.quote: to stop, from time to time as any such payment is made, the running of the time within which an action may be commenced upon the principal sum or upon any installment of principal or interest due on such note,
claims.note: The source identifies the principal sum and installments of principal or interest due on the note.

claims.claim: Each such payment starts a new period.
claims.quote: and to start the running of a new period of time, but no such payment of itself shall revive a cause of action once barred.
claims.note: The draft includes the once-barred limitation.

claims.claim: No such payment by itself revives a cause of action once barred.
claims.quote: but no such payment of itself shall revive a cause of action once barred.
claims.note: The limitation concerns the payment by itself.

claims.claim: The period for an action on a contract, obligation or liability founded on a written instrument is four years.
claims.quote:
Within four years:
(a) An action upon any contract, obligation or liability founded upon an instrument in writing, except as provided in Section 336a;
claims.note: The post-sale money judgment proviso is outside the stated scope.

claims.claim: The written-instrument rule is subject to the exception in Section 336a.
claims.note: The draft names the exception without asserting what Section 336a covers.

claims.claim: Once the Section 337 period has run, a person shall not sue, initiate arbitration or initiate another legal proceeding to collect the debt.
claims.quote: When the period in which an action must be commenced under this section has run, a person shall not bring suit or initiate an arbitration or other legal proceeding to collect the debt.
claims.note: The prohibition and its timing match subsection (d).

claims.claim: The Section 337 period may be extended only pursuant to Section 360.
claims.quote: The period in which an action may be commenced under this section shall only be extended pursuant to Section 360.
claims.note: The source expressly identifies Section 360 as the only basis for extension.

result.summary: The provided statutes support the claims within the stated scope. The draft distinguishes a qualifying promissory-note payment that restarts a running period from a payment that, by itself, cannot revive an already barred claim.
